answers.answer: NomNomzBot runs as an installation that you reach as a dashboard in your browser, and the bot answers in your chat. You start by either signing in to an installation someone already runs or installing your own with Docker. Then you choose Continue as broadcaster, open Commands in the Build group, make a schedule command and type !schedule in chat to test it. Step by step: 1 get the address or install; 2 open the address, press Continue as broadcaster and approve on Twitch; 3 press Commands in the Build group of the sidebar and make the command, using the linked page; 4 type !schedule in Twitch chat and press Enter. Every action the prose needs has a step.
answers.quote: You either sign in to an installation someone already runs, or you install your own.

answers.answer: To use an existing installation you need its address, and it helps to know whether it runs full or lite. To install your own you need Docker and a Twitch app, either your own or the shared NomNomzBot app. You sign in with your Twitch account. A moderator also needs the broadcaster to have signed in there first. All of this is stated in 'Choose how to start' and in 'The bot, the dashboard and your channel'.
answers.quote: You need Docker and a Twitch app.

answers.answer: After sign-in, the dashboard opens on your channel and the bot joins its chat. Your first task worked when the bot answers !schedule with your stream times. Without a bot account, that answer shows under your own Twitch name. The concepts are told apart this way: the bot is the part that stays connected and answers in chat, and the dashboard is the website where you set up what it does.
answers.quote: The bot answers with your stream times.

answers.answer: The moderator does not need to install their own bot. They ask the broadcaster or the person who runs the installation for its address. After the broadcaster has signed in there with Continue as broadcaster, the moderator list is copied from Twitch. The moderator then signs in with Continue as moderator and picks the channel under Channels you moderate in the channel switcher. The reason is that moderator access comes from the broadcaster's moderator list on that installation.
answers.quote: A moderator does not install a bot of their own.

answers.answer: Step 4 names the toggle Keep commands and rewards on while offline but does not say where it is. This did not stop me, because the broadcaster is answered while offline anyway, so the test still works. The cost is a moment of wondering whether you must find that toggle first. The lite-installation consequence in step 2 is also stated earlier, in 'Choose how to start', so I did not learn it too late.
answers.quote: While you are offline, it answers only you and your moderators, unless you turn on Keep commands and rewards on while offline.

answers.answer: In Next steps, 'line marker' is used without being explained on this page. A listener does not know what it is, but it only points to the linked page, so the cost is small. Nothing else sounded unnecessary when read aloud.
answers.quote: See which account the bot types from, and set its line marker, on Bot account.
